foreign drug laws and what fast food is called abroad. | Waiting in the corridor outside their target's flat, the two argue over whether a foot massage is worth killing a man for. | Marcus recites a passage of scripture and the pair shoot a young man named Tobin for double-crossing their employer, Otis, and recover a briefcase. | A fourth man hidden in the bathroom empties a revolver at them without hitting either, which Marcus calls divine intervention. | In the car afterwards Rollo's gun goes off and blows the head off their passenger Del. | Marcus parks the bloodied car at his friend Warren's house, where a fixer directs the cleanup and gives the men fresh clothes. | Over breakfast in a coffee shop, two small-time robbers decide on the spot to hold up the diner they are sitting in. | Marcus talks the robber down mid-holdup, hands over his own wallet, keeps the briefcase and lets the couple walk out. | The two hitmen deliver the briefcase to Otis at his bar, where Otis is paying the ageing boxer Denny to take a dive in the fifth. | Rollo buys heroin from his dealer Kip and shoots up before his night out. | Rollo takes Otis's wife Nadia to a themed diner where they win the dance contest. | Nadia snorts Rollo's heroin, overdoses, and is revived by an adrenaline shot to the heart on the dealer's living-room floor. | Denny double-crosses Otis, wins the fight and kills his opponent in the ring, then escapes in a taxi. | Hiding in a motel with his girlfriend Marielle, Denny discovers she has left his father's watch behind in his flat. | Denny returns for the watch and shoots Rollo dead with a submachine gun left on the kitchen counter. | Denny and Otis collide in the street, crash, and are taken prisoner in the basement of a pawnshop. | Denny breaks free, comes back with a sword from the shop wall while one of their captors is raping Otis, and Otis declares them square on condition Denny leaves town. | Denny collects Marielle and rides out of the city on a motorcycle taken from the pawnshop.

Martin kills one and is struck in the head, losing the ability to form new memories. | Martin builds a system of instant photographs, annotated notes and tattoos to hunt the second attacker, a man he knows only by the initials R.M. | About a year before the main action, a plainclothes officer called Roy helps Martin find and kill the real attacker, a killing Martin forgets within minutes. | In a motel room he cannot remember checking into, Martin narrates the Prine case down the phone to an anonymous caller. | Martin burns his wife's hairbrush and books in a field, trying to grieve a loss he can never retain. | The caller feeds Martin a name and a location, identifying the drug dealer Gil Marsh as the man he is looking for. | Martin beats and strangles Gil in a derelict basement and photographs the body. | As he dies Gil whispers "Elias", which Martin cannot explain, and Martin changes into the dead man's suit and takes his sports car. | Roy arrives and tells Martin that Gil was innocent, that Martin already avenged his wife a year ago, and that Martin is himself the man in the Prine story. | Rather than believe him, Martin burns the photographs of Gil, writes "he is lying to you" on Roy's picture and copies down Roy's licence plate as his next target. | Martin drives to a tattoo parlour and has the plate inked on his thigh as the sixth fact. | At her bar, Gil's girlfriend Corinne recognises the dead man's clothes and car and serves Martin a beer the staff have spat in. | Corinne hides every pen in her house, goads Martin into hitting her, then returns bruised and blames a man called Vance so that Martin will go after him. | Martin ambushes Vance in a motel bathroom, beats him and drives him out of town at gunpoint. | Corinne runs the licence plate through a friend at the vehicle registry and hands Martin a record naming Roy Mercer. | Martin lures Roy to the derelict building, shoots him in the head and photographs the corpse.

fabula: Tobias and Ivy meet at a beach party in a seaside town at the end of the rail line and break into an empty house on the shore. | Over two years they fall in love - the ice on the frozen river, the noodle house, the drive-in. | The relationship curdles into recrimination over Ivy's drinking and Tobias's withholding. | Ivy comes home drunk having dented Tobias's car, and the fight ends with her walking out for good. | Ivy hires a memory-erasure clinic to remove every trace of Tobias from her mind. | Tobias visits the bookshop and finds Ivy treating him as a stranger and flirting with a young man named Peck. | Nina and Grady show Tobias the form letter from the clinic, and he goes to its director, Dr. Hallam, demanding the same procedure. | Tobias boxes up every object connected with Ivy so that the clinic can map the memories attached to them. | The technicians Dell and Peck run the overnight erasure in Tobias's flat, and Peck pockets the mementos to use on Ivy. | Inside his own head Tobias watches the most recent and ugliest memories dissolve around him one by one. | Reaching the memories he loves, Tobias changes his mind and tries to smuggle Ivy into memories she was never part of. | Dell and the receptionist Rosa get high on Tobias's bed and lose track of the procedure as his map goes off the rails. | Dr. Hallam arrives to re-map the erasure, and Rosa kisses him - only for his wife to reveal that Rosa's own affair with him was erased. | In the last surviving memory, the empty house on the shore, Tobias and Ivy say goodbye and she tells him to meet her at the beach. | The erasure completes and Tobias wakes the next morning with no memory that Ivy ever existed. | Tobias skips work on an impulse he cannot account for, takes the train to the coast and meets Ivy on the frozen sand. | They drive back to the city together and she invites him up to her flat. | Rosa quits the clinic and mails the files and session tapes back to every patient on the books. | Tobias and Ivy listen to their own recorded voices tearing each other apart; she runs, comes back, and they agree to try anyway.

syuzhet_notes: Told-order bullets 1-2 are a false opening: they are chronologically the penultimate act, and only the closing scenes reveal that the couple have met before. Everything from told-order bullet 6 to bullet 17 takes place during the single night of the erasure, with the memories replayed in reverse chronological order - told-order bullets 9, 10, 13 and 15 are the memories themselves, running backwards from the break-up to the first meeting.
fabula_notes: The woman's own visit to the clinic is never dramatised; it is inferred from the form letter the friends produce. fabula: In a mining boarding house out west, Emmett Rusk's mother signs her son over to the banker Barrow after a defaulted lodger's mine deed makes the family rich. | The boy drives his sled into Barrow's stomach and is taken east away from his parents anyway. | On his twenty-fifth birthday Emmett takes control of the fortune and tells Barrow that of all his holdings he wants to run a failing city newspaper, the Clarion. | Emmett moves into the Clarion, installs his manager Marsh and his friend Devlin, and prints a signed statement of principles on the front page. | Emmett hires away the entire staff of the rival paper and throws a party with a brass band and a chorus line. | Emmett returns from a buying trip abroad engaged to Adele, the governor's niece. | A run of breakfast-table scenes charts the marriage cooling into silence behind separate newspapers. | Emmett meets the shopgirl Nora Kell on the street with mud on his coat and starts visiting her rooms in secret. | Mid-campaign for governor, the party boss Halloran brings Adele to Nora's rooms and threatens exposure, and Emmett refuses to withdraw. | Emmett loses the election, Devlin asks to be transferred to another city, and the marriage collapses. | Emmett marries Nora and forces her into an opera career for which she has no voice. | Nora's debut is a humiliation, and a drunk Devlin begins the savage review that Emmett finishes, prints, and fires him for. | Nora swallows poison rather than sing again, and Emmett finally lets her stop. | Emmett shuts Nora away in the half-finished palace he calls Silvermount, where she works jigsaw puzzles in the vast empty hall. | After a joyless beach picnic and a quarrel, Nora packs and leaves him. | Emmett wrecks Nora's bedroom, finds a glass snow globe, murmurs "Bluebell", and carries it past the endless mirrors. | Alone at Silvermount, Emmett dies with the word "Bluebell" on his lips and drops the snow globe on the floor. | A newsreel obituary recaps Emmett's public life and closes without explaining his last word. | The reporter Nash is sent to find out what "Bluebell" means and is turned away by a drunk Nora in a seaside nightclub. | Nash reads Barrow's memoir and interviews Marsh, Devlin, Nora and the butler Colm before concluding that no single word explains a life, as workmen shovel a sled marked Bluebell into the furnace.

fabula: Undercover officer Danny Roarke rehearses a fabricated anecdote about a drug bust in a public toilet with his handler Pruitt until he can tell it like a memory. | Danny performs the anecdote for the boss Bram, his son Cal and Mr. Ash, and is taken onto the crew as Mr. Elm. | Ren Vasco walks out of prison and reports to Bram and Cal, who owe him for the years he kept his mouth shut. | Over breakfast the crew argue about what a pop song is really about and whether waitresses deserve a tip. | Bram hands out the tree aliases and Mr. Birch objects to being Mr. Birch. | The robbery collapses within a minute, and Mr. Ash shoots his way clear of the police from the getaway car with Mr. Elm beside him. | Fleeing on foot, Mr. Elm hijacks a car and is shot in the stomach by the terrified driver, whom he shoots dead. | Mr. Ash drives the screaming Elm to the warehouse rendezvous, cradles him and swears he is not going to die. | Mr. Birch arrives, argues that the job was a setup with an informer inside it, and hides the diamonds outside the building. | Mr. Cedar strolls in and produces a kidnapped patrolman, Doyle, from the boot of his car. | Left alone with the bound officer, Mr. Cedar dances to a radio oldie, cuts off his ear and douses him in petrol. | Mr. Elm shoots Mr. Cedar dead from the floor and tells Doyle that he is a cop and that the police are waiting outside for Bram. | Cal returns, listens to Elm's account of Cedar, and shoots Doyle dead himself. | Bram arrives, names Mr. Elm as the informer, and Mr. Ash refuses to believe him and turns his gun on Bram. | The three-way standoff leaves Bram, Cal and Ash all shot, with only Ash and Elm still breathing. | Elm confesses that he is a police officer, Ash shoots him as the police storm the warehouse, and Ash is cut down.

syuzhet_notes: The present tense is the warehouse. Told-order bullets 4, 6 and 9-12 are flashbacks, each announced by a title card naming whichever man has just walked into the room, which hands the audience his backstory at that moment. The film opens on the breakfast and cuts straight from it to the bleeding aftermath.
fabula_notes: The interior of the robbery, including the shooting of the staff, is described in dialogue but never dramatised, so it is not listed as an event; only the escape from it is shown. The weeks between the informer's recruitment and the job are elided entirely.

syuzhet_notes: The film opens on told-order bullet 1, a scene from near the end of the story, then a title card announces that what follows happened the day before, and the rest runs as a largely forward-moving braid of intercut strands. The opening moment recurs in the last act at the point where the film catches up with it, so the discovery of the body is both the first and the sixteenth thing the audience sees.
fabula_notes: The strands overlap rather than following one another and the film offers almost no time markers, so the ordering within a given day is inferred from causal links - the shop is looted after the warning, the rescue follows the traffic stop. That the body in the opening scene is the detective's brother is withheld and only becomes legible in retrospect.

fabula: An insomniac product-recall investigator finds that the only thing that lets him sleep is crying at support groups for diseases he does not have. | Ada Vey starts attending the same groups, and her obvious faking destroys his release. | On a business flight the narrator meets soap salesman Rex Marrow and pockets his card. | The narrator's flat and all his catalogue furniture are destroyed in an explosion, and he calls Rex, who takes him into a derelict house at the edge of the industrial district. | Outside a bar Rex asks the narrator to hit him as hard as he can, and the two beat each other bloody in the car park. | What starts as two men brawling hardens into a weekly basement club with its own rules, pulling in more and more members. | Ada overdoses, Rex brings her back to the derelict house, and the two begin a loud affair the narrator cannot stand. | Rex renders fat stolen from a cosmetic surgery clinic into soap and sells it back to the department stores at eighty dollars a bar. | Rex burns the narrator's hand with lye and holds him there, refusing to let him retreat into meditation. | The narrator blackmails his employer into paying him to stay away, using his own beaten face as the evidence. | Rex turns the club into an organisation he calls Havoc, filling the house with shaven recruits who take orders and vandalise corporate property. | Rex steers the car into oncoming traffic, lets it roll, and then disappears. | A member of Havoc named Ogden is shot dead on an operation, and the narrator starts trying to shut the whole thing down. | Travelling city to city, the narrator finds identical clubs everywhere and men who greet him as Rex Marrow. | The narrator works out that he and Rex are the same person, and that Rex has been acting while he sleeps. | Ada confirms that she has been sleeping with him, not with a separate man. | The narrator discovers that Havoc has mined the towers of the debt-record companies and tries to defuse the charges. | Rex beats him down a stairwell in one of the towers, and the narrator puts a gun in his own mouth and shoots himself through the cheek to kill Rex. | Ada is delivered to the tower by the shaven recruits, and the two hold hands at the window as the buildings come down.

northern plains site. | Marion and physicist Cole Reddick enter the shell and make contact through the barrier with the two creatures they nickname Pike and Perch. | Marion takes off her hazmat suit to show the visitors a human face, and the two sides begin building a vocabulary out of circular written marks. | As Marion learns the circular language she starts having vivid, unplaceable visions of a daughter. | The twelve sites share their findings until one government's translation of the phrase "offer weapon" fractures the coalition and the exchanges stop. | Rogue soldiers plant a bomb inside an incurable illness, and Marion tells her that her father walked out after she told him something he could not accept. | Nella dies in hospital with Marion holding her.

fabula: Child psychologist Aubrey Lang and his wife Frida celebrate a civic award for his work with children. | A former patient named Emory breaks into their bathroom, accuses Aubrey of having failed him, shoots him in the stomach and then kills himself. | Aubrey bleeds to death on the bedroom floor with Frida beside him. | The following autumn Aubrey takes on nine-year-old Toby Salter, a withdrawn boy whose case reminds him of Emory's. | Toby's mother Dana keeps finding cupboards standing open, drawers pulled out and marks on her son's body that she cannot explain. | Toby is shut in a cupboard at a birthday party and comes out hysterical and bruised. | Aubrey arrives late for his wedding anniversary dinner and Frida leaves the restaurant without speaking to him. | Toby finally tells Aubrey that he sees dead people walking around who do not know that they are dead. | Aubrey almost drops the case, then replays the old tape of Emory and hears a terrified voice in another language behind his own. | Aubrey tells Toby to stop running from the ghosts and to listen to what they want from him. | Bree Marlow, a girl who has just died, appears in Toby's tent and hands him a videotape. | At Bree's wake Toby gives her father the tape, which shows her stepmother poisoning her food. | Toby tells his mother about the ghosts and repeats what his dead grandmother heard her say at the graveside, and Dana believes him. | No longer terrified, Toby is cast in the school play and is happy in it. | Aubrey tells Toby that he has helped him and that the two of them will not need to see each other again. | Aubrey goes home, watches his and Frida's wedding video, and sees that she is asleep and has been talking to no one. | Frida's hand opens and Aubrey's wedding ring falls out, and he finds the bullet wound in his own back. | Aubrey tells his sleeping wife that he loves her and lets go.

syuzhet_notes: The film runs almost strictly forward, and its single displacement is the one that matters: told-order bullet 17 is a flashback to the night of the shooting, suppressed for the whole runtime and released only in the closing montage, which also replays earlier scenes to show that nobody but the boy has spoken to the psychologist since. The nonlinearity here is one withheld event rather than a shuffled timeline.
fabula_notes: The psychologist's death is elided by a caption naming the following season, so the months between the shooting and the new case are inferred rather than shown. fabula: A travelling priest passes the soldier Davin and his veiled wife Sela on the forest road. | The bandit Korrin, dozing under a tree, watches them go by and glimpses Sela's face when the breeze lifts her veil. | Korrin lures Davin off the path with a story of buried swords and ties him to a tree. | Korrin brings Sela to the clearing and forces himself on her while her bound husband watches. | Sela demands that the two men fight to decide which of them she belongs to. | Korrin cuts Davin's bonds and the two fight clumsily and in open terror. | Davin is killed and Sela runs from the thicket. | Korrin takes the soldier's sword and horse and leaves. | A woodcutter stumbles on the body in the undergrowth, runs off to report it, and quietly takes the costly dagger with him. | A constable captures Korrin by the river after the stolen horse throws him. | At the court Korrin boasts that he killed the soldier in a magnificent duel of nineteen strokes. | At a temple Sela testifies that after the rape her husband looked at her with contempt, and that she fainted holding her dagger and woke to find it in his chest. | Speaking through a medium, the dead Davin says his wife asked the bandit to kill him, and that he took his own life with the dagger in his shame. | Sheltering from the rain under a ruined gate, the woodcutter and the priest tell a passing stranger that they cannot make sense of what they heard. | The woodcutter admits he saw the whole thing and describes a squalid, cowardly fight in which both men begged and the soldier died almost by accident. | The stranger points out that the woodcutter stole the dagger, which is why he lied to the court. | An abandoned baby is found under the gate and the stranger strips it of its clothes. | The woodcutter carries the baby home to raise with his own six, and the priest's faith in people comes back.

syuzhet_notes: The present is the ruined gate in the rain, which the film opens on at told-order bullet 1 and returns to for bullets 15-18. Everything between is flashback, much of it flashback inside flashback: the courtyard testimony is recalled at the gate, and the killing in the thicket is dramatised inside that testimony. Told-order bullets 5-11 are staged four separate times across the runtime, once per witness, with the facts changing every time; they are counted once here.
fabula_notes: The film refuses to settle which account is true, so any single chronology is a choice. This one follows the woodcutter's final version, generally taken as the least self-serving, and treats the four tellings of the killing as one event set. Whether the husband was killed by the bandit, by his wife or by his own hand is never resolved.

champion at everything and saves Hollow Creek from the giant Torvald by befriending him. | Errol and Torvald leave together and part at a fork in the road, Errol taking the hard path through the woods. | Errol stumbles into a hidden town called Willow, where nobody wears shoes and nobody ever leaves, and meets a little girl called Pella. | Errol leaves Willow anyway and joins the ringmaster Grubb's circus, working three years unpaid for one fact a month about a girl he glimpsed across the tent. | Errol learns the girl is Marguerite, fills a field with daffodils for her, and takes a beating from her fiance Byrne. | Errol marries Marguerite and is drafted into the war, where he steals secret papers and is carried home by a pair of conjoined singers. | Reported dead, Errol walks bait. | Humiliated, Sam stops speaking to his father for three years. | Errol goes back to Willow, finds it derelict and repossessed, buys the town to save it, and meets the grown Pella. | Sam, living fabula: Police and security services seal off the old square of a European city for a counter-terrorism summit. | In a television truck at the edge of the square, producer Dana Kroll directs the live coverage and argues with her crew over the shots. | Security officer Cale Brody, back on duty after taking a bullet for the head of state, works the crowd with his partner Renner. | A local policeman named Marco is drawn away from his post by his girlfriend Pilar, who is part of the plot without his knowing it. | A tourist, Gil Farrow, films the square on his camcorder and catches faces nobody else notices. | A double stands in for the head of state on the podium and is shot twice by a sniper. | Two devices detonate, one among the crowd and one beneath the platform, killing dozens. | Brody sees Marco running from the square and chases him through the streets, convinced he is a bomber. | Renner, secretly part of the plot, is exposed and shot dead by his own conspirators. | The mastermind Valero and his team take the real head of state out of a hotel safe room and drive him away in an ambulance. | Brody gets hold of Farrow's camcorder and identifies the conspirators on the footage. | Pilar learns that her brother Tomas has been forced into the plot by a hostage held over him, and she is killed. | Brody commandeers a car and chases the ambulance across the city. | Tomas is ordered to detonate his vest and refuses once he sees that his own brother is safe. | The ambulance swerves to avoid Farrow, who has run into the road after a lost child, and crashes. | Valero is shot dead, the head of state is pulled out of the wreck alive, and Brody collapses from his injuries.

syuzhet_notes: The film replays the same twenty minutes eight times, rewinding to the same moment with an on-screen clock at the end of each pass and handing the point of view to a different witness. Told-order bullets 1-11 therefore circle one short span of time instead of moving through it, and every rewind puts the film back behind the point it had just reached. Only from told-order bullet 12 does the story finally run forward to its end.
fabula_notes: Because the passes overlap almost entirely, this chronology orders material the film presents as simultaneous or repeated; several bullets are visible in more than one pass and are counted once here. What the real head of state is doing during the square scenes is withheld until the fifth pass.

The baker Otto Kemp takes an order for a birthday cake for a boy called Charlie Rill. | Charlie is knocked down by a car driven by a waitress called Rhona on his way to school and walks home insisting he is fine. | Charlie collapses into a coma, and his parents Grant and Elaine keep vigil at the hospital. | Grant's estranged father Duff turns up at the hospital and confesses an affair from decades ago. | Unpaid and ignored, the baker starts making anonymous menacing phone calls to the family. | Telephone-sex worker Cheryl talks men through their fantasies from her living room while her husband home. | Officer Rowe, cheating on his wife Peg with a woman called Nan, abandons the family dog to cover one of his lies. | Nan's ex-husband Cass, a helicopter pilot, learns she has a new man and saws her furniture to pieces. | Ike and Dot house-sit for the Hartigans and photograph Dot made up as a beaten corpse. | At the dinner party Bess admits to a long-ago nude modelling session and an affair, and Neil makes a scene. | Charlie dies in hospital, and Grant and Elaine go to the bakery to confront Otto, who feeds them warm bread and grieves with them. | Bee finds her mother asleep, closes the garage door and kills herself with the car engine running. | At a picnic in the hills Stu smashes a young woman's head with a rock. | A tremor shakes the entire city, and every death and every wreck is folded into one evening bulletin.

syuzhet_notes: The film braids nine loosely connected city stories that run at the same time rather than one after another, cutting between them constantly and often on a sound or a passing car. Because the strands are concurrent, most of the reordering is lateral - the film moves sideways between households rather than backwards in time - with the night spraying at told-order bullet 1 and the earthquake at bullet 20 bracketing everything in between.
fabula_notes: The strands are simultaneous and the film supplies almost no clock times, so the ordering across the three days rests on the few hard markers: the cake is ordered before the accident, the fishing trip runs across a weekend, the earthquake closes everything. The dead woman in the river is never identified or explained, and any connection between her and the last killing is left for the audience to draw.

fabula: Elliot Farb grows up in a house under a seaside amusement pier, depressed at nine because the universe is expanding. | At school Elliot kisses a girl in class, and his classmates stand up one by one to announce what they grew up to be. | Elliot does his army service entertaining troops and becomes a stand-up comedian in the city. | Elliot's first marriage, to Judith, fails while he obsesses over a political assassination in bed. | Elliot's second marriage, to Carol, fails amid literary parties and her refusal to be interrupted. | Elliot meets Peggy Rowan after a tennis game with his friend Max, and she drives him home terrifyingly and asks him up for wine. | Elliot and Peggy's first date ends in bed, and afterwards she needs a cigarette. | Peggy moves in with Elliot, who pushes her into adult-education classes and books about death. | Elliot sends Peggy to an analyst and pays for it, and their two sessions are played side by side in split screen. | Elliot and Peggy visit her family in a farm town, where her grandmother stares at him and he sees himself at the table as a figure from another century. | Peggy's brother Neil confides his urge to steer into oncoming headlights, and then drives them to the airport. | Elliot and Peggy break up, and each of them tries seeing other people. | Peggy calls Elliot at three in the morning about a spider in the bathroom, and they get back together. | Peggy starts singing in clubs and is courted professionally by the record producer Sy Kale. | Elliot and Peggy fly to the coast for a television award, and Elliot hates every minute of it. | On the flight back each of them concedes, in unspoken narration, that it has ended. | Elliot flies back to the coast to propose, is turned down in a health-food restaurant, and crashes a rental car. | Elliot writes a play in which the woman says yes, and admits to the audience that you can do that in art. | Elliot and Peggy meet again in the city as friends, and he watches her walk away. | Elliot tells the joke about the man whose brother thinks he is a chicken, and says relationships are irrational but we keep going through them anyway.

fabula: Between the wars, in a suburb outside the city, the novelist Vera Holt begins writing The Hostess while her husband Edmund and the servants manage her illness. | Vera's sister Nell visits with her children, and a dying bird is buried in the garden. | Vera tells Edmund at the railway station that she will die if she is kept in the suburb, and he agrees to move back to the city. | Vera decides that her heroine will live and that someone else - a poet - will die instead. | Years later Vera fills her coat pockets with stones and walks into the river, leaving a letter for Edmund. | In the post-war years, the pregnant housewife Hazel Fenn reads The Hostess in bed rather than get up for her husband Walter's birthday. | Hazel and her small son Robin fail at making a birthday cake and start it again from scratch. | Hazel's neighbour June comes to ask her to feed the dog while she goes into hospital, and Hazel kisses her. | Hazel leaves Robin with a sitter, takes a hotel room and lays out sleeping pills, and then decides to live. | Hazel comes home, gets through the birthday dinner, and leaves her family for good once the second baby is born. | In the present, Miriam Crest buys flowers for a party for her friend Gideon, a poet dying of an incurable illness who calls her by the name of the novel's heroine. | Miriam argues with Gideon, who will not be consoled and wants neither the party nor the prize. | Gideon's former lover Ansel visits, and Miriam breaks down in her kitchen over the summer they were all happy. | Miriam's daughter Fern and her partner Marnie watch her hold the whole day together. | Gideon tells Miriam he stayed alive for her, and lets go of the window ledge. | Hazel Fenn, now old, arrives from overseas for the wake and tells Miriam what she did and why. | Miriam lets Hazel stay the night, and Fern takes her upstairs. | Vera's letter to Edmund is read over all three women: to look life in the face, always, and to put it away.

syuzhet_notes: Three days spread across most of a century are cut together as though they were one day, matched on gesture and object - a vase of flowers, a kiss at a kitchen door, an egg cracked in one decade and caught in another. Told-order bullet 1 is a prologue from years ahead of the material that immediately follows it, and the film uses no captions at all, so every jump between the three periods is carried by hair, furniture and light.
fabula_notes: The three strands are not causally simultaneous but are cut as if they were, so a single chronology pulls apart scenes the film deliberately fuses. The link between the housewife and the dying poet - that she is his mother, and that the boy of the middle period is the poet of the present - is withheld until near the end, and it is what makes this ordering legible at all.

fabula: On a hot day one summer, thirteen-year-old Junia Thorne finishes a play to be performed for her brother's homecoming. | Junia watches from an upstairs window as her sister Rosalind strips to her underwear and climbs into the fountain in front of Tom Vasey, the housekeeper's son. | Tom drafts a letter of apology to Rosalind, sends the obscene version by mistake, and Junia reads it on the way. | Junia walks in on Tom and Rosalind making love in the library and takes it for an assault. | The twins run off, and during the search Junia sees their cousin Cissy being raped in the dark and names Tom as the man. | Tom is arrested and taken away in front of the family, and Rosalind breaks with all of them. | Five years later Tom is released from prison into the army and is separated from his unit in the retreat across the continent. | Rosalind, now a nurse in the city, writes to Tom, and the two spend a few hours together on his leave. | Tom walks to the evacuation beach with two corporals and reaches a shore of burning vehicles, shot horses and thousands of waiting men. | Tom lies down in a cinema on the seafront and dies of septicaemia the night before the ships come. | Junia, eighteen, takes a nursing place in the city instead of the university place she was offered, and treats men brought back from the continent. | Junia learns that Cissy is marrying Neville Frome, the man who actually raped her. | Junia goes to Rosalind's flat, finds Tom there, and promises to recant her statement and set the truth down in writing. | Rosalind is killed when a bomb bursts the water main above an underground station. | Decades later the elderly Junia, dying and giving her last interview, admits that she never went to the flat and that Tom and Rosalind never saw each other again. | Junia says she gave the two of them in her novel the life they were never allowed, and the film shows them together at a seaside cottage.

other the two boys join forces. | Nix watches Dinah dance alone through a peephole in the back of her father's delicatessen. | The boys begin rolling drunks and stash the proceeds in a case inside a station locker. | Sallo shoots Nino dead in the street, Nix knifes Sallo in return, and Nix is sent to prison. | Released years later, Nix finds Duke running a large bootlegging operation with Pilo and Squint. | The gang work for the union man Corrigan and the crooked police chief Vasari, whose newborn son they swap in the maternity ward. | Nix hires a deserted seafront restaurant for a night with Dinah, and rapes her in the car when she tells him she is leaving for the film capital. | The dry years end, and Duke, unwilling to stop, proposes robbing the federal bank. | Ruby and Nix agree that the only way to save Duke from himself is to have him arrested on a smaller job. | Nix telephones the police to tip them off, and is told at the scene that Duke, Pilo and Squint were shot dead and their bodies burned in the street. | Nix goes to the station locker for the gang's money, finds the suitcase empty, and leaves the city under another name. | In an opium den, Nix lies back and smiles at the ceiling. | Decades later Nix receives an invitation to the reinterment of his three friends in a mausoleum he never paid for. | Nix comes back to the city, finds Bunny still behind the delicatessen counter, and is given the key to the same locker. | Nix finds the mausoleum with his own name on the plaque and a suitcase of money inside, described as an advance on his next job. | Nix visits an aged Ruby at a retirement home endowed by Marrick, and she tells him Duke had wanted to die. | Nix finds Dinah backstage, now the cabinet minister Marrick's mistress, and she tries to send him away without letting him see her son. | Nix goes to Marrick's house and finds Duke alive, having stolen everything, now asking Nix to kill him. | Nix refuses to recognise him and walks away, and a garbage truck grinds past behind him as Duke disappears.

syuzhet_notes: The film cuts between three eras - boyhood, the bootlegging years and old age - without captions, carrying each jump on a sound or an object: a telephone that will not stop ringing, a thrown disc, a shot through a peephole. It opens in the middle era at told-order bullets 1-3, jumps decades forward at bullet 4, then all the way back at bullet 6, and thereafter alternates, so a childhood scene and an old man's return repeatedly sit side by side.
fabula_notes: The late-life frame may be an opium dream the protagonist is having in the middle era - the closing smile invites the reading and the film never settles it - and the ordering here takes the three eras as literally successive. The decades he spends hiding under another name are elided entirely, and his friend's survival is explained only in retrospect.

fabula: The assassin code-named Mantis leaves the Adder Unit for the child she is carrying and plans a wedding in a desert chapel under a new name. | Corvin and the rest of the unit walk into the wedding rehearsal and massacre everyone in the chapel. | Corvin shoots Mantis through the head, and she survives in a coma. | Reiko Sana, whose parents were murdered in front of her as a child, kills the boss responsible at eleven and grows up to be a top assassin. | Reiko takes the eastern capital's underworld by beheading a rival at a council meeting, and rules it with the schoolgirl killer Momo and the lawyer Delphine. | The one-eyed Dara comes to the hospital to kill the comatose Mantis with a syringe and is called off by Corvin at the last moment. | For four years an orderly called Wade sells the comatose woman's body to visitors. | Mantis wakes, kills Wade and his customer, and finds her belly flat and her baby gone. | She lies in the back of Wade's truck for thirteen hours until she can move her toes. | Mantis writes out her list of five names and drives to Odette Bray's house in the suburbs. | The two fight through the kitchen, break off when Odette's small daughter comes home from school, and Mantis kills Odette with a thrown knife in front of the child. | Mantis flies to a southern island and talks the retired swordsmith Ito into making her a blade to kill his own former student, Corvin. | In the eastern capital Mantis cuts Delphine's arm off outside a restaurant called the Lantern and sends her to Corvin as a message. | Mantis kills Momo and then fights her way through the Eighty across the restaurant. | Mantis duels Reiko in the snow garden and takes off the top of her skull. | She interrogates the maimed Delphine in the boot of a car and leaves her alive to tell Corvin everything. | Corvin asks Delphine whether Mantis knows that her daughter is still alive.

his birthday, which he takes as taunting from her killer. | Journalist Anders Sten loses a libel case against the financier Kolberg and resigns from his magazine. | Sonja Vik, a ward of the state and a researcher for a security firm, is handed a new guardian, Rask, after her old one has a stroke. | Sonja compiles the background report on Sten that persuades Gustav Ravn to hire him. | Gustav brings Sten out to the island to write a family history and, in truth, to find out who killed Ingrid. | Rask makes Sonja perform oral sex before he will release her own money. | Rask rapes Sonja at his flat, not knowing she has hidden a camera in her bag. | Sonja comes back, tasers Rask, marks him permanently as a rapist and blackmails him with the recording. | Sten works through the family archive, is shot at in the woods, and finds Ingrid's notebook full of names and numbers. | Sten's daughter Maja points out that the numbers are scripture verses. | Sten asks the security firm for a research assistant and is given Sonja, who has been reading his hard drive for months. | Together they match the verses to a series of ritual murders of women across the country going back forty years. | They trace the killings to Otto Ravn, Ingrid's father, and then to her brother Viktor. | Viktor catches Sten, chains him in a soundproofed basement and explains what he does down there. | Sonja arrives, splits Viktor's face with a golf club, and lets him drive away to his death in a crash. | Sonja nurses Sten back to health and the two become lovers. | A cousin called Karin, living overseas, turns out to be Ingrid herself, using the cousin's name since fleeing her father and brother. | Ingrid comes home to Gustav, and Sten has his story. | Sonja, in disguise, empties Kolberg's accounts at a foreign bank and feeds Sten the story that destroys him, then sees him with his editor Britt and throws away the present she had bought.

fabula: Leaflets fall on the port and enemy fire drives the private Ives through the streets to the beach, the only one of his patrol to make it. | Ives meets a silent soldier called Marne burying a body, and the two carry a wounded man onto a hospital ship to get themselves aboard. | They are put off the ship again, and it is bombed and goes down in the harbour behind them. | Ives, Marne and a corporal called Beckett hide in a beached trawler outside the perimeter, waiting for the tide to lift it. | Enemy soldiers use the trawler for target practice, and the men inside argue about throwing Marne overboard to lighten it. | The trawler floods and Marne drowns, and the survivors swim clear into a burning oil slick. | The harbour commander Dyer watches from the mole as ship after ship is sunk and the perimeter shrinks around the beach. | In the home port the civilian sailor Whitlock takes his boat Kestrel out himself with his son Nate and their friend Row rather than surrender her to the navy. | They pick a shivering soldier off the hull of a wrecked ship, and he panics when he learns where they are heading. | In the struggle Row is thrown down the ladder and blinded, and he dies later in the cabin. | Three fighters cross the water; the leader is shot down almost at once and the pilot Ryland takes over with a smashed fuel gauge. | His wingman Poole is hit and ditches in the sea, and his canopy jams as the aircraft fills and sinks. | Whitlock brings Kestrel alongside and Nate smashes the canopy in to pull Poole out. | Ryland shoots down the bomber attacking the minesweeper, saving the men in the water and on the mole. | Kestrel reaches the oil slick and takes Ives, Beckett and others aboard as the fuel catches fire. | Ryland, out of fuel, glides the length of the beach, brings down one more aircraft, lands past the perimeter and burns his fighter before he is taken prisoner. | The little ships arrive and the evacuation succeeds, and Dyer stays behind for the allied troops still waiting. | Ives and Beckett reach home expecting contempt and are handed beer and blankets, and Ives reads the prime minister's speech aloud from a newspaper.

syuzhet_notes: The film runs three strands at three different durations - a week on the mole, a day at sea, an hour in the air - and cuts between them as though they were simultaneous, so an aircraft ten minutes into its flight appears alongside soldiers who have been waiting for days. Told order and chronology therefore come apart continuously, and the film shows one event twice from two strands: the kill over the minesweeper is seen from the water before it is seen from the cockpit.
fabula_notes: Because the three strands cover different spans of time, putting them on one clock means deciding where the shorter ones start inside the longest, which the film fixes only at the moments the strands physically meet. The enemy forces are never seen, so their movements are inferred entirely from their effects.

fabula: As a young man scavenging in the closed city of Vyrsk, Yuri Sarkin finds a buried cache of gold and a message from the future, and is hired to assemble the Device. | In the future, the scientist who built the Device splits it into nine pieces, hides them in the past, and kills herself so that it cannot be rebuilt. | Dying of cancer, Sarkin decides to take the world with him by assembling the Device and reversing entropy. | An intelligence operative survives a siege at a concert hall and swallows a cyanide pill that turns out to be a loyalty test, and is recruited into the organisation. | The operative is shown inverted bullets and briefed by a scientist on objects whose entropy runs backwards. | He traces the bullets to the arms dealer Devi, who names Sarkin as the source. | An official called Ballard tells him to reach Sarkin through his estranged wife Ana, an art appraiser trapped by a forged painting she authenticated. | The operative and Vidal break into the airport freeport to steal the forgery and are attacked by a masked man moving backwards through the fight. | Ana introduces the operative to Sarkin, who tries to have him killed on the yacht. | Sarkin takes the operative along on a raid to seize a radioactive core from a motorway convoy in the coastal city. | The operative hides the case, Sarkin shoots Ana with an inverted bullet, and the operative gives up the case to save her. | The operative and Vidal invert themselves and drive the convoy chase backwards to recover the case, and the operative fights the masked man in the freeport - himself. | The inverted Ana is taken back through the freeport turnstile to be healed before the radiation kills her. | The team work out that Sarkin's dead-man switch will detonate the Device at the moment of his death, on a yacht off a southern coast days earlier. | A temporal pincer movement is mounted at Vyrsk, with one team moving forward and one backward through the same ten minutes. | On the yacht, Ana keeps Sarkin alive until the signal comes, and then kills him herself. | In the hypocentre, the operative and a soldier reach the Device, and a corpse with a red-tagged rucksack opens the gate for them. | Vidal reveals that he was that corpse, that he has known the operative for years from the other direction, and goes back to die. | The operative kills Devi to protect Ana and her son, and understands that he is himself the founder of the organisation who recruited them all.

fabula: As a young woman, Meilin defies her father Renjie to emigrate overseas with Bao. | Meilin and Bao open a laundromat, and every other life she might have had closes off one by one. | Their daughter Junie grows up feeling judged, and Meilin cannot bring herself to accept her girlfriend Robin. | On the origin branch, a version of Meilin invents branch-jumping and pushes her own daughter's mind across every universe at once until it shatters, making the entity Kavra Nul. | Kavra Nul builds a black ring, a hole made of everything that ever mattered, and starts hunting for the Meilin who can face her. | In the laundromat, Meilin prepares for a tax audit while Bao tries and fails to hand her divorce papers. | Renjie arrives from overseas for the new year party, and Meilin hides Robin from him. | In the lift to the tax office, the origin-branch Bao takes over her husband's body and gives Meilin an earpiece and a set of instructions. | Meilin branch-jumps for the first time in a supply closet and fights the security guards with skills borrowed from a film-star version of herself. | The auditor Beulah Sneed turns berserk, and the tax office becomes a battlefield. | Meilin is shown the origin branch and told that Kavra Nul is her own daughter. | Meilin jumps through lives she never lived - film star, opera singer, teppanyaki chef, a world where people have hot dogs for fingers, two rocks on a cliff. | The origin-branch Bao is killed, and Meilin's mind begins to come apart as she jumps too far. | Meilin confronts Kavra Nul, who says she does not want to kill her but wants her to see that nothing matters. | Believing nothing matters, Meilin turns on the people around her and nearly follows her daughter into the ring. | Bao, in every universe at once, asks her to be kind, and Meilin starts fighting with kindness instead. | Meilin gives each attacker what they actually need, wins Renjie's acceptance of Robin, and reaches Junie at the edge of the ring. | Meilin tells Junie that even if nothing matters she would still choose to be here with her, and pulls her back. | Back at the tax office the family files the return together, and Meilin's attention drifts for a moment across every universe at once.

fabula: As a boy at a religious school, Bruno Malvasi sneaks down to the beach to watch the prostitute Mareva dance, and is beaten for it by the priests. | Bruno's mother watches over him from the edge of every memory, and he loses her early. | Bruno becomes the country's most celebrated director, with a run of hits and a public that hangs on his every word. | Bruno marries the actress Renata, who gives up her own career for him. | Bruno takes a mistress, Gilda, and installs her in hotels near wherever he happens to be shooting. | Bruno's last two films fail, and he finds he cannot write the next one. | A press conference in the capital for the unwritten film Aurora turns into an ambush, and Bruno flees to a spa on the coast. | His costume designer and confidante Zita tells him plainly that he has nothing to say. | Gilda follows him to the spa, checks into his hotel and stages an elaborate seduction. | Bruno summons his muse, the star Adriana, and cannot tell her what the part is. | The producer begins erecting sets for a picture with no screenplay, while the crew idles on the lot. | Renata arrives at the spa and sees Gilda's name in the hotel register. | Told to leave, Gilda takes an overdose in her room and survives it. | Bruno imagines every woman in his life singing for him at once on an empty soundstage. | Renata confronts Bruno in front of the press and tells him she is done being his material. | Bruno abandons the film on the day shooting was to start, and the sets are struck. | Bruno spends two years in silence, until Zita talks him into trying once more. | Bruno calls Renata to a screen test for a film about the two of them, and she agrees to sit and watch.

syuzhet_notes: The present is the fortnight before a shoot that never starts, and it keeps breaking into two kinds of interruption: memories - told-order bullets 5, 7, 8, 10 and 12 - and staged musical numbers that happen only inside the director's head. The largest of those is told-order bullet 1, which opens the film on a soundstage that exists nowhere in the story.
fabula_notes: Several numbers are fantasy rather than event and have no fixed position in time; they are placed here at the moment in his life they draw on. His childhood, his mother's death and the arc of his career are recalled rather than staged as present action.

straight over. | Grigor the Nail tells Solly about a bookmaker's in the city and simultaneously tips off the pawnbrokers Ike and Benno to rob him there. | Boxing promoters Halloway and Digby send the fighter Pretty Sam to buy a caravan from a camp of travellers. | The bare-knuckle fighter Finn knocks Sam out over the deal, leaving Halloway without a man for the gang boss Coldstone's fixed bout. | Halloway has to put Finn in the fight instead, and promises Coldstone that Finn will go down in the fourth round. | Solly lands in the city, delivers the stone to the fence Hersch, and heads for the bookmaker's to bet on the fight. | Ike, Benno and Tulley bungle the robbery, take Solly's arm and his case, and are chased off by Grigor. | Finn knocks his opponent out cold in the first round, and Coldstone loses a fortune and takes it out on Halloway. | Marv flies in, finds Solly gone, and hires the bounty hunter Ledge to find him. | Grigor takes Solly, cuts off his arm to get the case open, handed in at a pet shop, coughs up the diamond, and Halloway and Digby end up holding it.

task force, which is in fact a front for the northern cartel. | Nuno helps capture the coastal cartel's enforcer Paz, who is tortured into naming the hit man Blanco. | Across the border, federal drug agents Brand and Dell arrest the mid-level dealer Nando Cano and turn him into a witness. | Cano's testimony brings the arrest of the importer Rafael Solis in front of his pregnant wife Nadia, who knows nothing about the business. | Judge Warren Bell is appointed the country's drug policy director and briefed in the capital on a war nobody there thinks can be won. | Bell's sixteen-year-old daughter Simone and her friends free-base at a party, and one of them nearly dies of it. | Nadia discovers that the family is bankrupt and that the cartel is threatening her son over her husband's debts. | Nadia goes to Rafael's lawyer Metz and then arranges a meeting with the coastal cartel's brothers herself. | Simone's habit moves from cocaine to heroin, and she is arrested and thrown out of school. | Nadia commissions Blanco to kill Cano before he can testify. | Bell tours the border, meets Obrero, and is told by everyone he talks to that treatment is the only thing that works. | Simone runs away and starts prostituting herself for drugs in an inner-city motel. | Blanco's car bomb kills Dell instead of Cano. | Bell abandons his official duties and searches the motels of his own state cannot fight a war against his own family. | Brand plants a bug at the party celebrating Rafael's release, Nadia takes over running the business, and Nuno watches the floodlit baseball game he asked for as his price.

real name of a courier for the fugitive leader, Nabil Rasheed, and the report is filed away and forgotten. | Two years later the analyst Reyna arrives at a secret site overseas and watches her colleague Kessner waterboard a detainee called Faris. | Broken by sleep deprivation and humiliation, Faris gives up the existence of a courier known only as Sahim. | Reyna works the detainee network for years, chasing the name through interrogations on three continents. | Bombings in a European capital and at a hotel in the region go off around her. | Reyna's colleague Fay cultivates an informant who kills her and six others with a suicide vest at a forward base. | Reyna survives an assassination attempt by gunmen outside her compound. | A detainee's account is matched against the buried report, and Sahim is identified as Nabil Rasheed. | Reyna has the courier's mother's phone tapped, and he is finally located in a northern city. | Surveillance follows the courier's white four-wheel drive to a fortified compound in a garrison town with no telephone line and no internet. | Reyna insists the compound is the fugitive leader's, and the agency director demands to know how certain she is. | The station chief and the analysts argue the probability down to sixty per cent, and Reyna says one hundred. | The government authorises a helicopter raid rather than an air strike, and two stealth helicopters are prepared. | A special-operations unit flies into the garrison town, and one helicopter's tail clips the compound wall as it lands. | The unit clears the house floor by floor, killing the courier, his brother and one of the leader's sons. | On the top floor they shoot the fugitive leader dead and carry the body out as the crippled helicopter is destroyed. | Reyna identifies the body in a hangar at a forward airfield. | Reyna boards a transport plane alone, is asked where she wants to go, and has no answer.

fabula_notes: Much of what is dramatised is conjecture presented as reconstruction - the film stages several versions of the shooting, only one of which can be true - so this chronology follows the account the prosecutor assembles rather than an established record. it, and use the profit to open a shop for Petra's designs. | Alone in her seafront flat, Golda is telephoned with news that she has been chosen to appear on a television game show. | Golda cannot fit into the red dress she wore to Davey's graduation, and starts a diet of grapefruit and hard-boiled eggs. | Davey and Cyrus make their first good buy, and the money starts coming in. | A doctor prescribes Golda amphetamines without examining her, and the weight starts falling off. | Petra breaks with her parents' money and starts drawing again, and she and Davey imagine the shop together. | Cyrus is caught up in a shooting at a street deal, and the supply dries up across the city. | Golda doubles her pills, starts grinding her teeth, and hallucinates the refrigerator advancing across the kitchen. | Davey's arm becomes infected at the injection site, and the three of them start using more than they can sell. | Petra sleeps with her psychiatrist Dr. Nolan for money to buy drugs. | Cyrus is arrested in a raid, and Davey spends the last of their money bailing him out. | Starving and alone, Golda hallucinates herself onto the game show and is jeered at by the studio audience. | Golda walks to the television company's offices in a stained coat and collapses in reception. | Davey and Cyrus drive south on a rumour of pure heroin, with Davey's arm turning black on the way. | Petra goes to a dealer called Ray and takes part in a sex party for a bag of heroin. | Golda is committed, force-fed and given electroconvulsive therapy while her friends wait outside the ward. | Davey's arm is amputated at a southern hospital, where the police are called about the needle marks. | Cyrus is put on a prison work gang, sick with withdrawal and dreaming of his mother. | Each of the four curls into the same foetal position - Davey in his bed, Petra clutching her bag, Golda staring at a screen, Cyrus in his bunk.

syuzhet_notes: The film is divided into three captioned seasons and moves forward through them, cutting between the mother's flat and her son's world often enough that the two declines run in step. Its nonlinearity is less reordering than compression and intrusion: montages of a few seconds stand in for weeks, and the mother's hallucinations at told-order bullets 8 and 13 are staged as though they were happening. The last movement cross-cuts all four collapses into one continuous sequence.
fabula_notes: Time passes in jumps marked only by the season captions, so the intervals between events are inferred rather than stated. The game show, the refrigerator and much of what the son sees are hallucination rather than event, and are placed here at the point in each character's decline at which they occur.

fabula: During a party at the house of his closest friend, a book agent named Wilder leads Odile to an upstairs room and tells her how lovely she is while the other guests drink downstairs. | Wilder and Odile rent rooms in a quiet district and fill them with linen and plates, giving the affair a household of its own. | Odile says she is carrying her husband's child, and the pair decide the rented rooms will go on exactly as before. | In a hotel abroad, her husband Emlyn asks about a letter held for her at the desk, addressed in a hand he recognises. | Odile confesses, and Emlyn remarks that he has always been fonder of his friend than of his wife. | Odile goes back to the rented rooms and says nothing whatever about the trip, and the afternoon passes exactly as the others have. | Emlyn drinks through a long restaurant lunch with Wilder, baiting him about contemporary fiction and never once mentioning what he has learned. | Over dinner at the married couple's house the two men discuss racquet games and schoolboy sport until Odile has no part in the talk at all. | Wilder and Odile decide the rented rooms have become a chore, split the crockery and surrender the lease. | In a bar two years afterwards, Odile tells Wilder her marriage is over and that she spent the previous night confessing everything to her husband. | Odile lets slip that Emlyn has been publishing a writer whom Wilder represents and whom the two men both quietly detest. | Wilder rings Emlyn in a state and Emlyn comes to his house the same evening. | Emlyn says he has known for four years, that his wife told him on the trip abroad, and that he never thought much of his friend's letters either.

fabula: At a works outing beside a stream, a young man sits away from the crowd with a girl from the packing line and tells her he intends to take photographs for a living. | The girl presses a tin of mints into his hand, and he watches a goods train pass with the feeling that everything is about to begin. | Called up, he is sent with his company to break a rising in a provincial city and takes a bullet through the calf. | Bleeding and terrified in the dark, he fires at a shape in a doorway and kills a schoolgirl who was trying to get home. | Years later, as a detective, he beats a student in a cell and finds that the work suits him. | The girl from the packing line brings him a camera she has saved up for; he refuses it and spends the night with a waitress. | He tortures an organiser in a country town, then washes his hands and sits down to a bowl of rice. | He marries a good-humoured woman he does not love and lets his colleagues arrange the whole wedding. | He runs a small furniture firm, strikes his wife, and learns she is sleeping with the man teaching her to drive. | He follows her, catches the two of them and beats the man, then returns to a mistress of his own. | The firm fails, his partner takes what money is left, and his wife walks out. | He buys a pistol and drives about the city unable to settle on who deserves it. | The husband of the girl from the packing line brings him to her hospital bed, where she is dying and cannot speak, and returns the camera she once bought. | He forces his way into a reunion picnic beside the same stream, climbs onto a railway bridge, and stands facing an oncoming train shouting that he wants to go back.

fabula: On a southern beach a woman notices a man who is holidaying at the same hotel with his girlfriend. | The girlfriend flies home after a row, and the man knocks at the woman's door that evening. | The two of them wade out into the sea together as the sun goes down. | At their wedding in a country hotel her estranged parents are seated at opposite ends of the table and every speech is cold. | He passes out drunk on the wedding night, and she lets a stranger in from the corridor. | Their son is delivered by emergency surgery while the father sits in the car park unable to make himself go inside. | He arrives on the ward hours later and admits where he has been. | Over dinner for his brother and his brother's boyfriend, he describes watching strangers have sex at a club. | She says at the same table that she was there and watched too, and the evening turns. | The couple begin sleeping in separate rooms, and he takes a lover at his office. | A clerk in a lawyer's office reads out the terms of the divorce and the two of them sign it. | They take a hotel room afterwards, sleep together one last time, and he dresses and leaves her lying on the bed.

fabula: A young man grows up in a small provincial town on the continent and qualifies in medicine. | He marries, and the child born to the couple dies as an infant. | He takes a post at an institute where the disabled are put to death by injection and by gas. | He is posted to a camp in the east and stands beside the senior physician during selections on the platform. | Inside the camp he performs dental procedures and experiments on the prisoners. | He takes a prisoner as a mistress and sends her to the chamber once he has tired of her. | The camp is cleared before the advancing army arrives and he walks west with forged papers in his coat. | He spends years in hiding on the southern coast under an assumed name, living quietly on gold. | He crosses the ocean under a second false name, given fresh papers by a clergyman who asks him nothing. | Working in hospitals abroad, he inflicts pain on his patients and persuades himself that he is curing them. | He carries on a long affair with a woman who never learns a single true thing about him. | He grows old under a third name, gardening, hoarding tinned food, and waking from dreams of a man in a white coat. | He collapses among his flowerbeds and dies in a hospital far from where he began.

fabula: Four sisters put on the eldest girl's play in the attic at Christmas and then carry their own breakfast down the road to a starving family. | The writer of the play meets the boy next door at a dance while hiding a scorch mark in the back of her dress. | The youngest sister is caned in front of her class over a jar of sweets and is withdrawn from the school. | The youngest burns her sister's manuscript, and is told she will never be forgiven as long as she lives. | The youngest goes through the ice on the river, and the sister who nearly let her drown forgives her. | The shy sister is given a dead child's piano by the old man next door. | A telegram reports their father wounded, and the eldest sells her hair to pay for their mother's journey to him. | The shy sister catches scarlet fever from the family they have been feeding and very nearly dies. | The second sister marries a poor tutor in the garden with almost no money and is glad of it. | The boy next door proposes and is refused, on the grounds that the two of them would destroy each other. | The writer sells lurid stories to a city paper under an invented name while a foreign professor at her lodging house tells her frankly that they are bad. | The youngest studies painting abroad under a rich aunt's eye and meets the boy next door again, drunk and aimless. | The married sister, poor now, buys dress silk she cannot afford and confesses it to her husband. | Word arrives that the shy sister is dying, and the writer goes home to nurse her beside the sea. | The shy sister dies, and the writer shuts herself in the attic and starts writing the story of the four of them. | The youngest and the boy next door marry abroad and come home together, and a letter offering herself to him arrives too late. | The writer argues the ending and the copyright out of her publisher, and the book goes to press.

fabula: A divorced woman comes back to her family's house in a river town with her boy and girl twins. | Her aunt makes it plain that she resents the twins and their mother equally. | A carpenter from the lowest caste works at the family's pickle works and is the twins' closest friend. | On the drive to meet a cousin from overseas, a man behind a cinema refreshment counter forces the boy to masturbate him. | The cousin arrives with her mother and the whole household makes a fuss of her. | The divorced woman and the carpenter begin meeting after dark on the far bank of the river. | The carpenter's father tells the family about the affair. | The woman is locked in her room and shouts through the door that her children are millstones round her neck. | The twins and their cousin row across the river in the dark, the boat turns over, and the cousin drowns. | The aunt tells the police that the carpenter took the children and raped their mother. | The police beat the carpenter almost to death in the ruined house across the river while the twins watch from a doorway. | The aunt makes the boy say the carpenter took them, and the carpenter dies in a cell. | The boy is sent away to his father, and his mother dies alone in a lodging house at thirty-one. | The grown daughter, divorced, returns to the river town and finds the house rotting and her great-aunt watching satellite television all day. | She finds her brother, sent back years before, walking in the rain and no longer speaking at all. | She goes to the ruined house across the river, now a heritage hotel where the old stories are performed for guests. | The twins stand together in the closed pickle works where the vats used to be. | Alone in the house at night, the twins sleep together.

fabula: A screenwriter three months behind on his payments is dodging the finance men who have come for his car. | He pitches a baseball picture at a studio and a young script reader tells the producer to his face that it is flat. | Fleeing the finance men, he blows a tyre and swings into the drive of a crumbling mansion on a famous boulevard. | Mistaken for the undertaker come to collect a dead chimpanzee, he meets a silent-era star nobody has thought about in twenty years. | She hires him to cut down the enormous script she has written as a vehicle for herself. | He moves into the room over the garage, and her butler fetches his belongings from his flat without being asked. | She buys him suits, a cigarette case and a watch, and the arrangement quietly becomes a kept one. | At a New Year party laid on for two she tells him she loves him, and he walks out to a friend's party instead. | The butler telephones to say she has opened her wrists, and he comes back and stays. | He starts slipping out at night to write a script with the young reader, who is engaged to a friend of his. | She drives to the studio with her script; a famous director is gentle with her, and the writer learns the studio only ever wanted to rent her car. | The butler admits that he directed her first pictures, that he was her first husband, and that he has been writing her fan letters himself for years. | She telephones the young reader, and he brings the girl to the house and tells her exactly what he is, so that she will go. | He packs, tells the old star the truth about her career and the letters, and walks out towards the pool. | She shoots him three times and he falls face down into the swimming pool. | With the police and the newsreel cameras filling the hall, she takes them for a film crew and descends the staircase ready for her close-up.

fabula: The lead barrister on a six-year class action defending a chemicals conglomerate stops taking his medication. | He strips during a deposition in a midwestern city and runs into the car park announcing that he is the servant of a corrupt design. | The firm's fixer, a ruined gambler, is sent out to bring him back. | The fixer, in debt to loan sharks over a failed restaurant, asks his partners for an advance against his bonus and is turned down. | The conglomerate's general counsel is briefed about the barrister and rehearses her answers alone in a hotel bathroom. | The barrister has obtained an internal memorandum showing the company knew its weedkiller was killing people. | He telephones one of the claimants and orders six hundred bound copies of the memorandum printed. | The general counsel authorises two contractors to put him under full surveillance. | The contractors kill him in his flat and dress it as a suicide by injection. | The fixer refuses to accept the suicide and finds the printer's receipt among the dead man's papers. | His brother's debts and his son's telephone calls close in on him from every direction at once. | He collects the annotated copy of the memorandum from the printers. | The contractors put a device in his car while he has stopped at the roadside to look at three horses in a field. | The car explodes, and he throws his watch and rings into the fire so the body will be taken for his own. | He confronts the general counsel at a board meeting, records her offering him money to keep quiet, and has the police waiting downstairs. | He gets into a taxi, hands the driver fifty dollars and tells him to just drive.

fabula: At a girls' day school, a mistress takes charge of a set of ten-year-olds and informs them that she is in her prime. | She teaches them about her dead fiance, about Italian painting and about her own opinions, in place of the syllabus. | She walks the set through the old part of the city and halts them in front of a queue of unemployed men. | The headmistress tries repeatedly to force her resignation and can find no grounds for it. | The art master, who has one arm, a wife and six children, kisses her in the art room. | She gives him up and takes the singing master as her lover instead. | She spends her weekends at the singing master's house on the coast with two of the girls attending as chaperones. | She decides that one particular girl shall become the art master's lover in her place. | The set's dull one, whom everybody blames for everything, leaves the school. | A different girl becomes the art master's lover, and discovers that every portrait he paints of any of them comes out looking like their teacher. | The mistress encourages a new girl to run away and fight in a foreign war. | The new girl is killed when her train is attacked, having gone to fight for the wrong side. | The singing master marries the science mistress. | The girl who became the art master's lover tells the headmistress that their teacher instructs in fascism, and hands her the grounds she has wanted for years. | The mistress is forced into retirement and spends the rest of her life trying to work out which of the set betrayed her. | The dull one dies at twenty-three in a hotel fire, running the wrong way along a corridor. | The mistress dies of an internal growth, and her betrayer, now an enclosed nun who has written a book on psychology, is asked through the grille what the chief influences of her schooldays were.

fabula: A virus let loose in the last years of the century kills most of the human race and drives the survivors below ground. | Decades on, the scientists running the underground colony send convicts up to gather specimens, and one of them volunteers. | He is sent back through time, arrives six years too early, and is arrested raving about a plague. | In the asylum a psychiatrist interviews him, and he meets the son of a celebrated virologist. | He is hauled back to the future and questioned about a recorded message the scientists have recovered. | He is sent to the right year and abducts the psychiatrist, who has since written a book about apocalyptic prophecy. | The two of them find graffiti for a shadowy group and trace the virologist's son to his father's estate. | The son denies everything and says the idea of stealing the virus was the convict's own, from the asylum. | The psychiatrist comes across a photograph from the first great war of a soldier who is unmistakably him. | He decides he has been mad all along and asks to be allowed to stay where he is. | She finds a bullet fired in the first great war in an X-ray of him and realises he has been telling the truth. | The shadowy group turn out to be animal rights activists who free the zoo animals and shut the virologist in a cupboard. | The pair go to the airport in disguise to stop the virologist's assistant, who is the real carrier. | She spots the carrier, he runs at the man with a gun, and airport police shoot him dead while a small boy watches from the concourse. | The carrier passes through the gate with the virus in his luggage, taking the next seat to one of the scientists sent back from the future.

fabula: A sound truck for a fringe presidential candidate circles the city broadcasting his platform to nobody in particular. | An ageing country star records a patriotic anthem while a foreign reporter drifts round the studio talking into a tape recorder. | The city's best loved singer collapses at her own airport welcome and is taken to hospital. | A pile-up on the freeway strands most of the city's musicians and hangers-on together for a whole afternoon. | A gospel singer performs with her choir while her husband negotiates with the candidate's organiser. | A folk trio records together while the man among them sleeps with women from every other storyline. | A quiet young man arrives in the city with a violin case and takes a room from an old widower whose wife is dying. | A waitress who has walked out on her husband keeps trying to get onto any stage that will let her sing. | A girl with no voice at all performs at a men's smoker and is made to strip for the room. | The best loved singer is discharged from hospital and breaks down on stage, rambling at the audience until she is led away. | The country star refuses to appear at the candidate's rally unless his own conditions are met. | The gospel singer sleeps with the folk singer after his set and goes home afterwards to her deaf children. | The widower's wife dies on the ward, and the young man lodging with him never notices. | The organiser assembles the rally by promising every performer something different. | The best loved singer performs at the rally and is shot in front of the crowd by the young man with the violin case. | The country star, hit in the arm, tells the crowd that this is their city and passes the microphone to the waitress. | The waitress gets her stage at last and leads the crowd in a song while the ambulances pull away. | The crowd goes on singing as the camera withdraws over their heads.

fabula: A doctor whose face was destroyed in the war sits in the lobby telling anyone passing that people come and go and nothing ever happens here. | A bookkeeper who has been told he is dying cashes in his savings and takes the most expensive room in the building. | A ruined nobleman working the corridors as a thief is pressed by his creditors for money he has not got. | A manufacturer arrives to close a merger that will collapse unless he lies about it. | A famous dancer refuses to go on, saying nobody comes to watch her any more. | The manufacturer engages a typist and makes clear what else the position involves. | The thief hides in the dancer's room to take her pearls and instead spends the night listening to her. | She discovers him there, and by morning the two of them are in love. | The bookkeeper loses his temper in the bar with the manufacturer, who is his own employer, and tells him precisely what he thinks of him. | The thief takes up with the bookkeeper and teaches him to drink and to dance. | The dancer performs better than she has in years and arranges to leave for the south with the thief in the morning. | The bookkeeper wins heavily at cards and then loses his wallet, and the thief, who took it, hands it back. | The manufacturer's merger collapses when the truth about the foreign contract comes out. | The thief breaks into the manufacturer's room for the money, and the manufacturer beats him to death with a telephone. | The manufacturer is arrested, the dancer leaves for her train believing her lover will follow, the bookkeeper takes the typist away with him, and the doctor repeats that nothing ever happens.

closes on the gate it opened at.

detonates. | The merger goes through, and the men who engineered the whole of it are photographed collecting a prize.

fabula: On the hottest morning of the year a disc jockey opens his broadcast from a storefront window on the block. | A young man gets out of bed at his sister's flat and goes off to deliver pizzas. | The pizzeria owner opens up with his two sons, the elder saying he hates the neighbourhood and everybody in it. | The block's old drunk buys his first beer of the day and is scolded for it by a woman watching from her window. | A regular objects that the photographs on the pizzeria wall are all of the owner's own countrymen and asks where the black faces are. | The owner throws him into the street, and he starts calling for a boycott that nobody joins. | A big quiet man walks the block all day with a boombox playing one song at full volume. | Three older men sit under an umbrella opposite a Korean grocery and talk about the block from morning until night. | A stammering man works the corner selling hand-coloured photographs of two murdered leaders. | The delivery man tells the owner's elder son to his face that every one of his heroes is black. | The old drunk pulls a child out of the path of a car, and the woman at the window softens towards him. | The hydrant is opened and the whole block plays in the water until a police car pulls up. | The big man and the boycotter come into the pizzeria at closing with the radio at full volume, demanding the wall be changed. | The owner smashes the boombox with a baseball bat and the fight spills into the street. | Police arrive and kill the big man with a chokehold in front of the entire block. | The delivery man throws a rubbish bin through the pizzeria window and the crowd burns the place down. | In the morning he comes back for his week's wages, and the two of them argue over the money among the ashes.
