fabula: Four young men say their prayers in a hotel room, and again in the departure lounge before they board. | A regional traffic centre notices an aircraft has stopped answering and picks up a hijacker's voice on the frequency. | The national operations centre starts tracking the aircraft that has gone quiet. | The first aircraft hits the north tower, and the controllers watch it on a television without believing what they see. | Passengers for the fourth flight take their seats and wait out a long delay on the tarmac. | The military sector is ordered to scramble fighters and cannot be told where to send them. | The second aircraft hits the south tower on live television. | The national centre orders every aircraft in the country onto the ground at once. | The third aircraft hits the defence headquarters outside the capital. | The hijackers aboard the fourth aircraft kill the pilots, take the cockpit and turn back east. | Passengers get through to families and answering machines on the seat phones and piece together what has happened elsewhere. | The passengers agree among themselves that the aircraft will not be allowed to reach wherever it is pointed. | Fighters are launched at last, unarmed, with no clear authority to bring anything down. | The passengers charge up the aisle behind a drinks trolley and force their way towards the flight deck. | The man at the controls rolls the aircraft and puts it into a dive. | The aircraft comes down in open farmland.

fabula: A boy is born in a small industrial town and grows into a weak, peculiar child. | His father throws him into the deep end of a pool to teach him to swim, and he sinks to the bottom. | He is conscripted as a chaplain's assistant and shipped overseas with no training worth the name. | He is lost behind the lines with a scout who beats him for wanting to be left to die. | The pair are captured, and the scout dies of gangrene on the prison train, blaming him with his last breath. | He is held in a camp beside enemy officers who have been drawing double rations for years through a clerical error. | He is sent on to a great city and housed with other prisoners in a disused abattoir. | The city is destroyed by fire in one night, and the prisoners in the meat locker come up to find it gone. | The prisoners are made to dig bodies out of the cellars until one of the diggers dies of the dry heaves. | A fellow prisoner promises to have him killed one day on the dead scout's account. | He comes home, collapses, and is hospitalised, where another patient introduces him to a hack science fiction writer. | He marries the daughter of the man who owns the optometry school and becomes rich. | He survives an air crash in the mountains, and his wife dies of exhaust fumes driving to the hospital. | He is taken by aliens and kept in a zoo on their planet with a film actress. | The aliens explain that every moment exists at once and that free will is an idea peculiar to his own planet. | He goes on a radio talk show and tries to tell the world about the aliens and the fourth dimension. | His daughter decides he is senile and takes his affairs out of his hands. | He is shot dead by a beam weapon after addressing a crowd, exactly as he has always known he would be.

syuzhet_notes: The narration jumps without warning between the war, the marriage, the alien zoo and the death, often mid-paragraph and several times a page. It is not a frame with flashbacks and not two alternating strands; the sequence is associative and says so itself.

fabula: A bombardier arrives on the island base and flies his first missions. | A gunner is hit over a target town and dies in the bombardier's arms as he finds the second wound under the flak suit. | The colonel raises the number of missions required to go home, then raises it again, and again after that. | The bombardier reports sick with a liver complaint just short of jaundice and stays in hospital as long as the doctors permit. | He censors the enlisted men's letters out of boredom and signs them with a borrowed name. | An investigator arrives to look into the forged signatures and turns up nothing whatever. | The squadron doctor explains that asking to be grounded for madness proves sanity, and is therefore grounds for nothing. | The mess officer builds a syndicate trading across both sides of the front and corners an entire country's cotton crop. | The mess officer contracts with the enemy to bomb his own squadron for an agreed fee. | One unfailingly cheerful patient empties the ward of every other man in it. | A idealistic airman is tried for an offence nobody can name, and later flies into a cloud and is never seen again. | The squadron doctor is recorded as dead because his name was on a flight manifest, and no paperwork can restore him. | A young airman falls in love with a prostitute who is asleep every time he calls on her. | The young airman is killed over a coastal target, and his prostitute blames the bombardier and tries to knife him wherever he goes. | The military police clear out the apartments, and the bombardier walks back through the city alone past one atrocity after another. | A fellow officer rapes and kills a maid and is not arrested, while the bombardier is arrested for being in the city without a pass. | The colonel and his second offer the bombardier a bargain: say the squadron is wonderful and go home a hero. | He refuses the bargain, learns that a lost comrade rowed all the way to neutral waters, and sets out to follow him.

fabula: A career thief serves nine years in prison abroad while his daughter grows up without him. | The daughter moves to the west coast and takes up with a wealthy record producer. | She works out that he is laundering drug money and threatens to go to the police. | His head of security kills her and dresses it as a crash on a canyon road. | The thief is released, reads a newspaper cutting somebody has posted to him, and flies out. | He finds an acquaintance of his daughter's, who tells him the little he knows. | He goes to a warehouse to ask questions, is beaten and thrown into the street, and walks back in and kills everyone in it. | He meets his daughter's old acting teacher, who tells him exactly what sort of father he was. | He and the acquaintance watch the producer's house from the hills above it. | He gatecrashes a party at the house, and the security men drive him into the desert to shoot him. | He kills the men in the desert and walks back out to the road. | The producer runs to a beach house up the coast with his young girlfriend. | The two men drive north, and the acquaintance is shot dead in the assault on the beach house. | The thief corners the producer on the rocks, and the producer admits the girl died out of his own panic. | He lets the producer live, flies home, and thinks about a day at the seaside with his daughter as a small child.

syuzhet_notes: The telling cuts one conversation across three different places and times at once, and drops shots of the journey home into scenes that come before it. There is no stable present: the same exchange belongs to several moments.
fabula_notes: The chronology is recoverable from the plot mechanics - the release, the journey, the deaths - even though almost no shot sits cleanly inside a single moment.

fabula: A boy with a stammer is treated by a hypnotist on television and speaks one clear sentence for the first time. | Decades earlier a young mother sits on a fence outside a country house waiting for a husband who never comes. | A doctor passing along the road stops to talk to her, and the fence collapses under the pair of them. | A barn burns at dusk while the family stand in the doorway and watch without moving. | The mother runs through the rain to the printing house certain she has let a fatal misprint through, and finds she has not. | The father comes home on leave during the war, and the children are shy of him. | The mother takes her son to sell her earrings to a doctor's wife in a warm house, and cannot make herself do it. | At a training camp a boy who has lost his entire family refuses an order and lies down on a grenade. | The grown son's own small boy, alone in the flat, reads a letter aloud to a woman who is not there. | In the present the son quarrels with his former wife down the telephone about their child. | He watches his mother, old now, cross a field with two children. | He lies ill in a darkened room while the doctors agree there is nothing physically wrong with him. | He remembers a girl at school with a cracked lip whom he could never bring himself to speak to. | A gust of wind crosses a field of buckwheat towards the house, and nobody indoors remarks on it. | An elderly woman walks two children over a meadow in the failing light as the camera draws back among the trees.

fabula: A young woman is taught by nuns that there are two ways through a life, the way of nature and the way of grace. | She marries, and their first son is born. | Two more sons follow, and the three boys run wild through the summers of a small southern town. | Their father drills them in discipline at the dinner table and teaches the middle one the guitar. | Their mother plays with them on the lawn while the father is away on business. | The eldest, jealous and confused, breaks a neighbour's window and steals a slip from a woman's drawer. | The eldest takes his brother into the yard, persuades him to put a finger over an air rifle, and shoots him. | The father loses his job when the plant closes and the family have to give up the house. | The eldest asks his brother's forgiveness in a doorway without managing to say any of the words. | A telegram reports that the middle brother has died at nineteen, and the mother cannot be consoled. | The father tells his eldest that he was too hard on all of them. | Galaxies condense, stars burn out, a planet cools, and something first stirs in its oceans. | A wounded creature lies in a river bed while another sets a foot on its head and then lets it live. | The eldest, a middle-aged architect in a glass tower, cannot get through the anniversary of his brother's death. | He walks through a doorway standing alone in a desert and finds everyone he has lost gathered on a shore.

fabula: As a young conscript a soldier lands on the coast with an armoured column. | His unit fires all night at a car approaching a roadblock and finds a family inside it at first light. | A comrade swims out to sea from a burning landing craft and lives when the rest of his unit does not. | Another soldier dances with a machine gun down a boulevard under sniper fire, beneath posters of an assassinated leader. | The unit shells an orchard and a boy carrying a rocket launcher is killed in front of them. | The soldier and two others bathe in the sea at night under flares while the city burns behind them. | Armed irregulars go into the refugee camps while the soldiers outside send up flares to light the sky for them. | Over two days the militia kill the people in the camps, while the soldiers on the roofs fail to grasp what they are watching. | The soldier stands at the edge of the camp as the women come out screaming. | More than twenty years on, a friend tells him over a drink about a recurring dream of twenty-six dogs. | He realises he remembers nothing whatever of the war and sets out to find the men he served with. | A psychologist explains to him that memory can be assembled out of what a person needs rather than what occurred. | A television reporter tells him what he saw in the camps and what he said to the defence minister on the telephone. | He understands that the flare-lit memory of himself in the sea is a screen he built to stand between himself and the camps.

fabula: A girl is brought to a farm in the border states and chooses one of the men there for herself. | The man's mother is bought out of slavery by his extra labour and settles in a house outside a northern city. | A new owner the slaves nickname after his schooling arrives and starts measuring them and writing them up in a ledger. | The young woman overhears him instructing his nephews to list her animal characteristics on one side of the page and her human ones on the other. | The men at the farm lay a plan to run for it, and the plan falls apart. | The nephews hold her down in the barn and take her milk while her husband watches from the loft and loses his reason. | Pregnant and beaten, she walks north alone, and a white girl delivers her baby in a beached boat. | She reaches the house and has twenty-eight days of freedom, and her mother-in-law holds a feast for ninety people. | The owner comes to the house to take her and the children back. | She carries the children into the woodshed and cuts her elder daughter's throat with a handsaw. | She is jailed and released, her mother-in-law takes to her bed and dies, and the neighbours stop calling. | Her two sons run away from a house haunted by the dead baby. | One of the men from the farm arrives after eighteen years and drives the ghost out of the house. | A young woman walks out of the water, gives the dead child's name as her own, and comes to live with them. | The man is moved out of the house room by room and is finally taken to bed by the visitor in the shed. | An old friend shows him the newspaper cutting about the killing, and he leaves. | The visitor swells and consumes the mother, until thirty women come into the yard and sing until she is gone.

fabula: In a border town a married mother of four meets a farmer and the two begin an affair in a trailer out in the fields. | Her eldest daughter discovers the affair and follows her mother out to the trailer. | A gas leak sets the trailer burning and both the woman and the farmer die in it. | The daughter is left to bring up her younger sisters while her father drinks and blames himself. | The farmer's son comes to the town to look at the wreck and to find out who the woman was. | The two children of the dead recognise each other and, out of grief more than anything else, become lovers. | The girl burns down her own family's house with her father's photographs inside it. | She finds she is pregnant, and the two of them run away together. | The boy is badly injured when their car leaves the road, and she is told he has died. | She gives birth to a daughter, leaves the baby with the boy's family, and vanishes. | Under another name she runs a restaurant on the northern coast, sleeps with men she does not know, and cuts herself. | The boy, alive and badly scarred, works as a crop duster with his own small daughter beside him. | He crashes his aircraft, and the child is brought north by a friend to look for her mother. | The friend finds the restaurant owner and tells her that the boy is alive and that her daughter is with him. | She flies south, and mother and daughter meet in a hospital corridor.
